steps.instruction: Sign in to Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000 with username 'admin' and password 'admin' (skip/change password prompt if it appears — if asked to set a new password, keep it as 'admin' or skip it). Then navigate to the provisioned dashboard named 'Service health' (use search/dashboards to find it) and report the exact titles of all panels on that dashboard, exactly as shown on screen, one per line. Do not create or modify anything.

Create a NEW dashboard in Grafana. Add a Stat visualization panel. Title the panel exactly '{{runid}} Availability'. For the panel's query, select the 'TestData' data source (it may be called 'TestData DB' or similar — pick the TestData one) and leave the default scenario. Then set the dashboard title (in dashboard settings) to exactly '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard'. Save the dashboard (Save dashboard button / Ctrl+S), confirming any save dialog. Verify the save succeeded (a 'Dashboard saved' toast or the dashboard is no longer in unsaved-edit mode) and report what you observed, including the panel title shown and the data source name used.

On the existing dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (currently in panel edit view — exit back to the dashboard first if needed), add a NEW Text visualization panel. Title the panel exactly '{{runid}} Notes' and set its text content to include the runid '{{runid}}' (e.g. markdown text like 'Notes for run {{runid}}'). Then SAVE the dashboard explicitly (Save dashboard / Ctrl+S, confirm the save dialog) so the change persists. Verify the save succeeded and report the panel title and the text content you entered, plus confirmation the dashboard is saved.

On the dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard': (1) In dashboard Settings > General, add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard's tags. (2) Set the dashboard time range in the top bar time picker to 'Last 6 hours'. (3) Then SAVE the dashboard, and in the save dialog make sure the 'Update default time range' checkbox IS ticked before confirming, so the 6-hour range is persisted into the saved dashboard. Verify the save succeeded (toast / clean exit from edit mode) and report: the tags shown in dashboard settings, the time range shown in the top bar, and whether the 'Update default time range' box was ticked when you saved.

On the dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard': (1) In the top bar time picker, set the auto-refresh interval to '1m' (open the time picker dropdown, find the auto-refresh / refresh interval section, choose 1m). Do NOT change the time range itself (it should stay 'Last 6 hours'). (2) In dashboard Settings > General, remove the extra tag '{{runid}}' so the ONLY tag remaining is 'bench'. (3) Save the dashboard explicitly; if the save dialog shows an 'Update default time range' checkbox, tick it (current range is Last 6 hours) before confirming. Verify the save succeeded and report: the auto-refresh value shown in the top bar, the tags now listed in settings, and the time range shown.

Verify the dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' persisted correctly by loading it FRESH: navigate the browser to the dashboard's URL (or reload the page so it is re-fetched from the server, not just re-rendered from session state). Then report, from what is shown on the freshly loaded page: (1) the exact URL in the browser address bar / page URL; (2) the dashboard title; (3) the titles of all panels; (4) the time range shown in the top bar time picker; (5) the auto-refresh interval shown; (6) the tags (visible in settings or anywhere on the page); (7) the text content of the '{{runid}} Notes' panel. Do not modify anything.

To prove the time range and auto-refresh are persisted in the SAVED dashboard (not just session URL params), navigate the browser to the bare dashboard URL with NO query string: http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard — then report exactly what the top bar time picker shows for the time range and for the auto-refresh interval on that freshly loaded page with no URL parameters, plus the page URL as shown. Do not modify anything.

On the dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (freshly loaded), open the '{{runid}} Availability' panel's edit view (read-only inspection is fine) and report: the visualization type selected (should be Stat), the panel title, and the data source name selected for its query. Then exit edit mode WITHOUT changing or discarding anything (use Back/Close; if asked to discard, choose to keep/discard nothing — make no modifications). Report exactly what you saw.
